https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/v5.4/esp32p4/api-reference/peripherals/lp_i2s.html (LP I2S on ESP32-P4 works as an I2S slave only and provides an RX channel only — no TX channel, no DMA)
https://www.espressif.com/sites/default/files/documentation/esp32-p4_datasheet_en.pdf (Ch. 2.3.2 LP IO MUX Functions Table 2-5 + Ch. 2.4 LP Peripheral Signals Routed via LP IO MUX)
scope:
Standard UART0-4, HP I2C0-1, SPI2 standard master (plus the optional quad-mode WP = IO2 / HD = IO3 lines), LEDC channels, ADC1/ADC2, RMT channels, I2S master, plus the LP UART, LP I2C, LP SPI and LP I2S controllers; other SPI hosts and high-speed modes not modeled. ADC1 covers GPIO16-23 and ADC2 covers GPIO49-54, per the ESP-IDF soc/esp32p4 adc_channel.h header and the P4 datasheet Analog Functions table — note that the ESP-IDF GPIO summary page labels GPIO49-54 as ADC1_CH8-13, which contradicts the driver header; the header/datasheet mapping is used here. RMT channels are modeled as one GPIO per channel without TX/RX direction.

Display/Camera peripherals: (1) camera0 = DVP 8-bit Camera interface routed through GPIOMatrix (same as ESP32-S3 LCD_CAM CAM DVP channel). (2) camera1 = MIPI CSI-2 2-lane receiver with dedicated differential pads: CLKP/CLKN + DATAP0/DATAN0 (lane 0 required for 1-lane mode), DATAP1/DATAN1 (lane 1 optional for 2-lane mode), refclk (output from P4, optional GPIO) and xclk/csi_enable/dvp_enable (optional GPIO-level control pads). MIPI pads are in VDD_MIPI_DPHY dedicated I/O domain, NOT routable through GPIOMatrix. (3) lcd0 = RGB LCD parallel interface (same as ESP32-S3 LCD_CAM, up to 24-bit d0-d23 + pclk/vsync/hsync/de), GPIOMatrix routed. (4) lcd1 = MIPI DSI 4-lane (clock lane + 4 data lanes), DPHY dedicated differential pads with dedicated I/O domain; lane 0 required for 1-lane mode, lanes 1/2/3 optional for wider busses; te (Tearing Effect) input and reset optional GPIO. ISP/H.264 and LP_CAM are not modeled here. twai0-twai2 model the three TWAI (CAN) controllers (TX/RX required, BUS-OFF/CLKOUT optional) routed through GPIOMatrix; an external transceiver is required. sdmmc1 models SDMMC host slot 1, which is GPIOMatrix-routed (any GPIO) with a 1-bit baseline clk/cmd/d0 and an optional 4-bit extension d1-d3; slot 0 is dedicated to UHS-I and is not GPIO-matrix routable, so it is not modeled.

LP peripherals: lpuart0 = LP UART (TXD/RXD required, CTSN/RTSN/DSRN/DTRN optional) and lpi2c0 = LP I2C (SDA/SCL open-drain). Both are driven by the low-power CPU and reach ONLY the low-power domain pads GPIO0-15 (VDD_LP / VDD_BAT) through the LP GPIO matrix, so every LP signal carries an explicit gpio allow-list limited to GPIO0-15; the default LP IO MUX pads are LP_GPIO14 (LP_UART TXD) and LP_GPIO15 (LP_UART RXD). The LP UART is a separate controller from UART0-4 and does not consume one of those instances. lpspi0 = LP SPI, a four-wire controller (LP_SPI_CK/CS/D/Q) on the same LP GPIO matrix and therefore also limited to GPIO0-15; the LP GPIO matrix exposes both an input and an output path for each of the four lines and ESP-IDF v5.4 ships no LP SPI driver, so the lines are modelled role-agnostically (direction "bidirectional") and no master/slave role is asserted. lpi2s0 = LP I2S, which ESP-IDF documents as slave-only with an RX channel only (no TX channel, no DMA access), so bclk/ws/din (LP_I2S_I_BCK/I_WS/I_SD) are inputs fed by an external I2S master and its output-side paths (LP_I2S_O_BCK/O_WS/O_SD) are not modelled. LP_CAM is not modelled.

signals.description: LP UART transmit (LP_UART_TXD). Reachable only on the low-power domain pads GPIO0-15 via the LP GPIO matrix; the default LP IO MUX pad is LP_GPIO14 (GPIO14).
LP UART receive (LP_UART_RXD); default LP IO MUX pad LP_GPIO15 (GPIO15).
LP UART request-to-send (LP_UART_RTSN, active low, optional).
LP UART clear-to-send (LP_UART_CTSN, active low, optional).
LP UART data-set-ready (LP_UART_DSRN, active low, optional).
LP UART data-terminal-ready (LP_UART_DTRN, active low, optional).
LP I2C data line (LP_I2C_SDA) on the low-power domain pads GPIO0-15.
LP I2C clock line (LP_I2C_SCL) on the low-power domain pads GPIO0-15.

LP SPI clock (LP_SPI_CK). Routed through the LP GPIO matrix, so it can only reach the low-power domain pads GPIO0-15 (VDD_LP/VDD_BAT); the LP GPIO matrix exposes both an input and an output path for this line, so its pad direction follows the controller role.
LP SPI chip select (LP_SPI_CS), optional, on the low-power domain pads GPIO0-15.
LP SPI data line D (LP_SPI_D), optional, on the low-power domain pads GPIO0-15.
LP SPI data line Q (LP_SPI_Q), optional, on the low-power domain pads GPIO0-15.
LP I2S bit clock (LP_I2S_I_BCK), driven by the external I2S master: the ESP32-P4 LP I2S works as an I2S slave only. Reachable only on the low-power domain pads GPIO0-15.
LP I2S word select / LRCLK (LP_I2S_I_WS), input from the external I2S master.
LP I2S serial data input (LP_I2S_I_SD); the ESP32-P4 LP I2S exposes an RX channel only (no TX channel, no DMA access).

USB D- on the USB1P1 pads shared with the USB Serial/JTAG controller (datasheet USB1P1_N0 = GPIO24). The full-speed USB 2.0 OTG alternate pair is GPIO26/GPIO27 and its D-/D+ roles may be swapped in hardware.
USB D+ on the USB1P1 pads shared with the USB Serial/JTAG controller (datasheet USB1P1_P0 = GPIO25).
